title: Middlegame blunders that drop material or ignore threats

explanation: Most of the lost points come from single moves in the middlegame that leave a piece en prise or ignore an opponent's threat. One such move can undo 20 moves of decent play. The cause is probably not checking what the opponent's last move attacks before making your own move.

title: Missing checks (yours and the opponent's) and king safety
evidence: The 'missed_check' motif appears 3 times and 'allowed_mate' once. Game 142, 16... b6 lost 952 cp (best was Qc3+). Game 142, 17... Qxa2 lost 343 cp (best was Qb4+). Game 141, 15... Nb4 lost 263 cp (best was Qa5+). Game 141, 18... Rg8 lost 543 cp and allowed mate (best was Qa5).
explanation: Checks are forcing moves, so missing them is costly. In several positions a check was the best move, and the player chose something quieter. In one case the player also allowed a mating attack.
how_to_improve: Make 'checks, captures, threats' your first scan on every move, for both sides. List every check you have, even ones that look pointless, and see where each leads. Then list the opponent's checks and threats against your king. When your king is exposed or the opponent's queen is near it, treat every move as dangerous until you have checked their forcing replies.
ai_review_note: 4 cited moves with large losses (952, 343, 263, 543 cp); 3 missed checks plus 1 allowed mate. Numbers and best moves are consistent. Concrete CCT habit.
